chapter.heading: If You Were in My Shoes
chapter.v: Job replied,

“I've heard
all this before. You are comforters who just cause trouble!

Will your
windy speeches never cease? What's bothering you that you have to answer me?

I could
talk like you do if you were in my place, stringing words together to criticize you, ridiculing you with a toss of my head.

I could
build you up by my mouth speaking words; the movement of my lips would ease your pain.

For me,
if I speak it doesn't ease my pain, and if I don't speak the pain is still there.

God, you
have worn me out. You have destroyed my whole family.

You have
made me shrivel up, which is a witness against me; my thin body testifies against me.

He has
torn me apart in his anger; in his hostility he has gnashed his teeth at me; my enemy pierces me with his fierce look.

People stare
at me with their mouths wide open, they slap me on my cheeks to mock me, they crowd around me to attack me.

God has
handed me over to evil people; he has thrown me into their hands.

I was
living in peace and he smashed me to pieces. He grabbed me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He set me up as his target.

His archers
surround me. His arrows pierce my kidneys without mercy. He pours out my gall on the ground.

Like a
wall he breaks me down, breach upon breach, rushing at me like a warrior.

I have
sown sackcloth to cover my skin; my strength lies broken in the dust.

My face
is red from crying and dark shadows surround my eyes,

although I
have done nothing wrong and my prayer is pure.
chapter.heading: The One Who Represents Mortals Before God
chapter.v:
Earth, do
not cover up my blood. May my cry find no place to hide.

Look, right
now my witness is in heaven; the one who speaks for me is on high.

My friends
scorn me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.

I want
my witness to speak for me with God as someone does for their friend.

For in
a few short years I shall go down that road from which I shall not return.”
